messages:
nadia-ic: Hey team — heads up Im planning to work from Mexico for ~45 days (Feb 3-> Mar 19). Wanted to check: does WFH stipend keep paying? Any benefits or insurance gaps I should worry about? Also concerned about triggering any payroll/tax registration for Redwood.

taylor-peopleops: Hi @nadia-ic thanks for flagging. Policy allows up to 30 days without additional review; >30 requires People Ops + Finance review and usually a payroll hold while we assess. Please fill the Remote Work Abroad form and select Mexico, and include exact dates and if youll meet with any customers or partners while there.

quinn-legal: Quick note from legal: 45 days may create different compliance signals in certain Mexican states depending on local rules. We need to know if youre doing any paid contract work for a Mexico-based company or meeting customers in-person. If neither, risk is lower but not zero.

liam- finance: From payroll/tax perspective: Mexico has rules around permanent establishments and local payroll withholding if an employee is present for extended periods, or if they perform services for local entities. 45 days is borderline; we'll consult our cross-border tax advisor. If advisor flags it, we may need to run payroll locally or issue a temporary contractor invoice — both are rare but possible.

anna-healthcare: Benefits/health insurance: our US group health plans have limited coverage abroad. For travel under 30 days, emergency care is covered but routine care is not. For 45 days, you could be out of network for a longer period. We can add short-term travel medical coverage at company rate if needed, or reimburse for reasonable emergency care. Please tell us your dates and whether you need extended coverage.

nadia-ic: No customer meetings, purely personal travel and remote work. Im on the standard US medical plan, and monthly stipend $150. My manager @kevin-eng approves this in-thread. Ill submit the form today. Any chance the stipend pauses while Im abroad?

taylor-peopleops: If your legal home base stays the same and you remain on US payroll, monthly WFH stipend typically continues for temporary travel. Because this crosses 30 days well do a payroll risk check; if payroll team needs to suspend stipend pending review, we'll notify you before payroll close.

liam- finance: We'll flag your payroll record and run the advisor check. If they advise no local registration, stipend continues and no payroll change. If they advise registration, well reach out to discuss options (local payroll vs. short-term contractor vs. changing travel plans).

payroll-bot: Reminder: Remote Work Abroad form must be submitted at least 7 business days before travel for reviews that may require external tax counsel. Submissions within 7 days risk payroll/benefits interruptions. :warning: 

quinn-legal: Also upload passport name + dates and confirm if youll be working from multiple Mexican states. Different states have different thresholds for social security or commercial activity.

nadia-ic: Thanks everyone. I submitted the form and attached travel dates and passport. No state hopping, staying in Mexico City the whole trip. Kevin approved.

anna-healthcare: Got your request. We can provision short-term travel health coverage for the 45 days; its an optional company-covered add-on for trips >30 days. If you want it, reply here and we'll process.

nadia-ic: Yes please add the travel coverage. Appreciate the quick responses.

liam- finance: Noted and starting advisor consult. Expect update within 48-72 hours. If anything changes well DM you and loop People Ops.

kevin-eng: Approved from manager side. Thanks for checking ahead.

payroll-bot: Update: payroll risk flag created for user nadia-ic. Hold placed on stipend changes pending review. You'll be notified of any payroll impacts.
